title: Engineering career, West Coast and move to Peoria
summary: From 1919 he worked for his father's firm in California, went to Texas oil fields, then joined a friend's business in Peoria in 1925; he heard no New Orleans music on the coast.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Then, uh, how long were you around New Orleans from 1919?

Well, I was in New Orleans from 1919 until 1920, a year, and then I went out to Pacific Coast and joined my father's firm as an engineer, which I had studied at school, but had not graduated as, because of the war. I spent a year out in California, and went back to New York to collaborate in a report we made for the Standard Oil Company problems. And then when that was through, they, they told me that the officers that they were sending a crew, which I was supposed to go with, to Athens, Greece. And I'd just come back from over on the other side, and I didn't want any part of it anymore, so I went home. And I stuck around New Orleans for about four or five months, and friends of mine that I've known, and fraternity brothers, decided to go to Texas oil fields and make a fortune, which we didn't make. And I came back to New Orleans, and, uh, heard from another friend of mine in Peoria, Illinois, that he was in, he was engaged in a business that he liked to have me join up, and I went up and saw him, and decided to go into business with him. And it's a business in which I'm presently engaged in.
Is that, for that long you've been? Yeah. That would have been the early twenties.
Uh, you mentioned the West Coast. Anybody there that impressed you as New Orleans-style musician?
No. I didn't hear anything out there.
What part of the West Coast were you in?

I was, um, most of the time in San Francisco. Uh-huh. And, uh, did some work for the, uh, firm in, uh, the southern oil fields of California, around, uh, New Hall, and, uh, the Murphy Coyote, uh, leases, and Los Angeles and Bakersfield.
